number.why: The served HR 0.61 with 95% CI 0.46–0.82 matches the reported older-adult primary cardiovascular composite for rosuvastatin versus placebo. This confirms the numerical HR, not an RR or the claimed prespecified analysis. The quoted subgroup results do not explicitly establish ITT status or a trial-end timepoint.

quotes.span: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive 20 mg of rosuvastatin daily or placebo.

The primary end point was the occurrence of a first cardiovascular event (myocardial infarction, stroke, arterial revascularization, hospitalization for unstable angina, or death from cardiovascular causes).

The rates of the primary end point in this age group were 1.22 and 1.99 per 100 person-years of follow-up in the rosuvastatin and placebo groups, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.61 [95% CI, 0.46 to 0.82]; P < 0.001).

entry.why: The older subgroup explicitly consists of randomized participants aged at least 70 without cardiovascular disease, so its clinical population is established. The parent trial admitted younger participants, and the subgroup was exploratory rather than prespecified. PARTLY captures these limitations; choosing the age cut-point after completion does not establish that subgroup members were not randomized.

quotes.span: Among the 17 802 participants randomly assigned with low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels less than 3.37 mmol/L (<130 mg/dL) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels of 2.0 mg/L or more without cardiovascular disease, 5695 were 70 years or older.
Inclusion Criteria: * Men 50 years or older, women 60 years or older
Effect estimates from this exploratory analysis with age cut-point chosen after trial completion should be viewed in the context of the overall trial results.

missed: The ruling conflates retrospective subgroup selection with absence of randomized participants meeting the clinical entry criteria. The population and limitation quotations above support partial alignment with the question while refuting prespecification; they do not justify discarding the established age and cardiovascular-disease status.
